title: Add sourced ontology file with validating test and decision entry
summary: Retry of the rejected ontology job (Olympus decision 5) for Sri and the verifier: add docs/ontology.toml with the seven seeded misread terms, a Rust structural test, a decision entry and a changelog line. The earlier failure was the repo vocabulary test (athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where) flagging "operator" in docs/design/job-planning.md. That word is absent at base, so the new text must simply avoid the banned words.

defaults_applied.how: The structural test is Rust; the data file is TOML read by it.
New test with negative cases; cargo test, clippy and fmt must be clean.
Ontology and docs written for outside readers, avoiding banned vocabulary.
Every term carries sources that the test checks exist.
No email or personal data in any file.
Criteria check the test running and content of the terms, not just file existence.
The producer runs the full suite, including policy tests, before handover.
Baseline-check feature left out as a separate change.
cargo test, clippy and fmt --check are the independent checks.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Typed request 'try again' takes precedence: this is the ontology retry, with the earlier user corrections (seven seeded terms, no per-occurrence BRIEF.md check) still applying.
The proposed baseline-comparison feature for job verification is a separate, larger change and is not part of this job.

At base, grep finds no 'operator' (any case) under docs/, so job-planning.md needs no edit unless the producer's own edits introduce the word; the producer must run cargo test (including xtask policy tests) before handover and avoid the banned vocabulary in all new text.
Audience: Sri, other agents reading the file, and the independent verifier running cargo test.

Hermes entry covers both senses (Hermes Agent, second studied system, Part 2 S1; Hermes the Orchestration god in the Olympus Pantheon in BRIEF.md). System is Olympus; Athena is its strategy and learning role; Sri owns Olympus.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/ontology.toml defines the seven terms (planning, job, Athena, Hermes, product versus system, landed, Sri). Each has a definition, the misread that caused it, a sources field naming existing paths or decision ids, and relations whose targets are all defined terms.

The Hermes entry names both senses (Hermes Agent, Part 2 S1, not part of Athena; Hermes as Orchestration god in the Olympus Pantheon, BRIEF.md), says which is part of Olympus, and cites a source for each 'not part of' claim.
Relations match Olympus: the system is Olympus, Athena is the strategy and learning role within it, Sri owns Olympus. No relation makes Athena the whole system.

The file states a term is added only when it causes a misread and how a check reads it (parse path and fields). Landed means merged on main through a verified pull request. The Sri term says use the name or 'they', never he or she, and cites job 20261017-173504-91ys. No per-occurrence BRIEF.md cross-check exists.

docs/decisions.md has a new entry keeping the ontology, citing the Olympus 2026-10-17 decision sheet (decision 5), listing alternatives (no ontology; per-study glossaries only), and stating studies keep their own concept model so firstmate, Hermes Agent and Athena are compared in the same terms. docs/decision-links.toml is updated if required and CHANGELOG.md has an entry.

Run `cargo test --locked`: the whole suite passes, including the new ontology test on docs/ontology.toml, in-memory negative tests (missing sources field, non-existent source, dangling relation target, duplicate term), and xtask's athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where. Run `cargo clippy` (clean) and `cargo fmt --check` (passes).
No secrets or personal data, including the user's email address, appear in any new or changed file.

out_of_scope: Baseline-versus-main comparison of check results in job verification (separate job).
Per-occurrence cross-checks of term names in BRIEF.md.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, or the xtask policy test's banned word list.
departures: Slightly higher pass probability than reference: the earlier failure cause is known (banned word) and the prior corrections are settled. Slightly lower acceptance because the proposed next request bundled a baseline feature that this reading leaves out.
